title: Grab and Move softlocking its trigger key when window is foreground
summary: New 0.102.3101 evidence narrows a useful control: a left-Alt tap on the desktop can latch Alt, and turning off only Alt-menu prevention restores normal input while Grab and Move stays enabled. This supersedes the earlier fullscreen-only evidence gap, without proving both reports share one mechanism.

next_action.label: Compare Alt tap with menu prevention on and off
next_action.reason: Physical releases produce balanced logical state in both option settings, without accidental Win+Alt shortcut activation.

judgment.rationale: New 0.102.3101 evidence narrows a useful control: a left-Alt tap on the desktop can latch Alt, and turning off only Alt-menu prevention restores normal input while Grab and Move stays enabled. This supersedes the earlier fullscreen-only evidence gap, without proving both reports share one mechanism.
evidence: The original report describes lost key-down delivery in fullscreen contexts on 0.100.2 and recovery on the desktop.
The attached report records Grab and Move in Win-modifier mode, Alt absorption enabled, game suppression disabled and normal startup logs only.
The November 16 commenter reproduces on the desktop using the laptop keyboard; Win+R behaves as Win+Alt+R after a left-Alt tap.
Their selective control disables only 'Prevent Alt from activating the window menu after moving or resizing'; the original author also reports related Win-modifier symptoms.

Current ReleaseModifierSession replays an unconsumed absorbed Alt down and chains the physical up; HandleKeyboardEvent tracks absorbed/replayed state: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/82bd57f5d23ee19a98b0c46f42c304742a7db426/src/modules/GrabAndMove/GrabAndMove/main.cpp
Preserve the existing public investigation trace: https://github.com/MuyuanMS/PowerToys/issues/616
judgment.recommended_action: Physical releases produce balanced logical state in both option settings, without accidental Win+Alt shortcut activation.

proposed_fixes.title: Reproduce the desktop Alt-tap control with both configured activation modifiers and record only modifier down/up ownership and replay counts.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: absorbed modifier replay and physical release become unbalanced; the Alt-option control identifies a narrower path but does not establish exact event ordering or equate it with every fullscreen case.
plan: Reproduce the desktop Alt-tap control with both configured activation modifiers and record only modifier down/up ownership and replay counts.
If replay causes logical latching, balance the synthetic transition with the actual physical up and handle partial SendInput failure without releasing genuinely held keys.
Test untouched Alt taps, real window gestures, focus changes, both Alt sides and Win activation independently.
verification: With Alt-menu prevention enabled, an untouched left-Alt tap leaves Alt released and Win+R remains Win+R.
Real move/resize gestures still suppress unwanted menus, while normal shortcuts and physically held modifiers remain intact.

actions.label: Compare Alt tap with menu prevention on and off

reproduce.title: Verify Grab and Move report
prerequisites: Grab and Move enabled where applicable
setup: Use a disposable session and no recording shortcut as the primary state observer; inspect modifier state without capturing typed content.
Keep Grab and Move enabled and begin with the commenter's Alt-menu prevention option enabled.
steps: 1. Press and release left Alt without moving any window; inspect logical Alt state.
2. Repeat with only Alt-menu prevention disabled, leaving the module enabled.
3. Repeat under Win and Alt activation modes, with laptop versus external keyboards and a simple fullscreen control.
4. Compare the original fullscreen loss separately; do not assume the desktop control proves the original sequence.
reproduce.expected_result: Physical releases produce balanced logical state in both option settings, without accidental Win+Alt shortcut activation.
